rachel_z: quick report - sampleapp upload is intermittently duplicating POSTs and sometimes crashing after a 401+refresh on Android 15. Repro steps + logs below.

devin_t: can you paste minimal repro and stack?

rachel_z: repro: 1) start UploadActivity -> large multipart upload streaming from FileInputStream, 2) server returns 401, 3) Authenticator does blocking refresh, 4) toggle network (airplane mode) during refresh. Outcomes seen: either two POST requests land after refresh (duplicate uploads) or crash: IllegalStateException: request body is not repeatable. Logs: 

```
2026-03-22 11:04:10.102 D/OkHttp: --> POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/upload
2026-03-22 11:04:10.301 D/OkHttp: <-- 401 https://api.redwood.ai/v1/upload (199ms)
2026-03-22 11:04:10.302 D/Auth: refresh token start
2026-03-22 11:04:10.520 I/Network: airplane mode toggled
2026-03-22 11:04:10.840 D/OkHttp: --> POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/upload (replay)
2026-03-22 11:04:10.840 D/OkHttp: --> POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/upload (duplicate)
2026-03-22 11:04:10.842 E/OkHttp: java.lang.IllegalStateException: request body is not repeatable
```

rachel_z: stack points to RetryAndFollowUpInterceptor.createRequestWithUpdatedAuth -> our streaming RequestBody is single-use so replay fails. Client stack: Retrofit with suspend CallAdapter v2, OkHttp Authenticator that invokes tokenProvider.refreshBlocking(), okhttp client has retryOnConnectionFailure(true).

nate_h: two interacting behaviors here: (A) OkHttp Authenticator will transparently re-issue requests by building a new request from response.request after auth update; (B) Retrofit coroutine adapter v2 can create/clone underlying Calls and coroutines' cancellation/resume semantics can lead to multiple Call instances if not carefully coordinated. Combined with network flaps this yields duplicates.

devin_t: what's the simplest short-term mitigation we can ship in sampleapp?

rachel_z: short-term we tried two mitigations: 1) move refresh out of Authenticator into an Interceptor with a single-flight refresh (AtomicReference<CompletableDeferred> pattern). This prevents OkHttp from running its transparent retry logic and lets us control when to re-issue requests; 2) implement a ReplayableRequestBody helper that caches the body to disk when stream is larger than a threshold so it can be replayed safely. Both reduced duplicates and avoided crashes in my local runs.

nate_h: can you paste the single-flight sketch?

rachel_z: pseudo:

```
val inFlight = AtomicReference<CompletableDeferred<String>?>(null)
val token = tokenStore.current()
val req = chain.request().newBuilder().header("Authorization","Bearer $token").build()
val resp = chain.proceed(req)
if (resp.code == 401) {
  val deferred = inFlight.get() ?: CompletableDeferred<String>().also { if (!inFlight.compareAndSet(null, it)) it.cancel() }
  val newToken = runBlocking { deferred.await() } // temporary; better: suspend-friendly interceptor
  return chain.proceed(req.newBuilder().header("Authorization","Bearer $newToken").build())
}
return resp
```

rachel_z: runBlocking is ugly but avoided OkHttp Authenticator threads doing network IO. The deferred is completed by a single refresh coroutine started once.

devin_t: and the ReplayableRequestBody?

rachel_z: simple wrapper that writes the incoming stream to a temp file the first time writeTo() runs and then reads from that file on subsequent writeTo() calls. Only enabled for bodies > threshold to avoid extra IO for tiny files. Clean up after request completes.

nate_h: longer-term SDK suggestions: 1) provide an official TokenRefreshInterceptor (suspend-friendly) in the Android SDK so users don't need to implement runBlocking hacks; 2) provide a ReplayableRequestBody utility (opt-in) with configurable disk threshold; 3) in onboarding docs call out "Authenticator vs Interceptor" caveat + interactions with retryOnConnectionFailure and Retrofit coroutine adapter v2; 4) consider changing the SDK default for Android clients to `retryOnConnectionFailure(false)` or at least document its side-effects for streaming uploads.

devin_t: agree. Also add a sampleapp e2e that toggles connectivity mid-refresh to prevent regressions. We should measure perf impact of ReplayableRequestBody and provide guidance.

devex-bot: Created ticket RED-DEVEX-3420: "TokenRefreshInterceptor + ReplayableRequestBody + docs + sampleapp e2e". Repro and patch candidate attached. <https://redwood.internal/issue/RED-DEVEX-3420>

rachel_z: I'll open a PR with (A) sampleapp opt-in ReplayableRequestBody, (B) Interceptor single-flight example, and (C) a short doc blurb for SDK onboarding. Will tag infra and docs.

nate_h: thanks — please also add a short note for engineers using suspend CallAdapters: ensure the CallFactory preserves request identity and don't recreate Calls on resume unless cancelled.

rachel_z: will add that. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
